questions.q: The correct decreasing order of acidity is:
questions.explain: Formic acid (pKa 3.75) has no electron-releasing group; benzoic acid (4.19) has COOH on a more electronegative sp² carbon; acetic acid (4.76) is weakened by the +I effect of CH₃.

questions.q: Which dicarboxylic acid has the lowest pKa₁?
questions.explain: Among these, the two COOH groups are closest in malonic acid (pKa₁ 2.85), so the second COOH withdraws electrons most strongly. Succinic (4.21), glutaric and adipic acids are progressively weaker.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most acidic?
questions.explain: The inductive effect fades with distance: the 2-chloro acid has pKa 2.86, the 3-chloro 4.05 and the 4-chloro 4.52, almost back to butanoic acid.

questions.q: Which order of acidity of the methylbenzoic (toluic) acids and benzoic acid is correct?
questions.explain: The ortho methyl twists COOH out of the ring plane and cuts ring-to-carboxyl resonance donation, so o-toluic acid (3.9) beats benzoic acid (4.2); the m (4.3) and p (4.4) isomers are weaker than benzoic acid because CH₃ donates electrons.
